concepts.why: The patient presented with classic symptoms of appendicitis, including intermittent throbbing abdominal pain that localized to the right lower quadrant, moderate tenderness in the right lower quadrant, and a positive Rovsing sign, which are all supported by facts F02, F04, and F05.
The biopsy of inflamed areas demonstrated foci of endometriosis, which is a key finding that supports this diagnosis, as stated in fact F10.

The repeat CT showed small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum, likely secondary to an adjacent pericecal soft-tissue mass, which is a clear indication of this condition, as described in fact F12.

The contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve, and the appendix was not identified, which could suggest an inverted appendix, as mentioned in facts F07 and F08.
The repeat white-cell count was elevated, and the CT showed a pericecal soft-tissue mass, which could indicate a neoplastic process, as suggested by facts F11 and F12.
The biopsy of inflamed areas demonstrated foci of endometriosis, which is consistent with intestinal endometriosis, as stated in fact F10.

The patient presented with signs of peritonitis, including inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve and mild inflammatory changes of the terminal ileum, as described in facts F07 and F09.
The diagnostic laparoscopy showed mild inflammatory changes of the terminal ileum and adhesions, which is consistent with this diagnosis, as mentioned in fact F09.

rationales.F01: The patient's symptoms are non-specific and could be related to various conditions.
rationales.F02: The localization of pain to the right lower quadrant is suggestive of appendicitis or other conditions affecting the terminal ileum.
rationales.F07: The presence of lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve is highly suggestive of appendicitis.
rationales.F08: The absence of the appendix on imaging suggests that it may have been removed or is not visible due to other conditions.
rationales.F10: The presence of endometriosis on biopsy is highly suggestive of intestinal endometriosis.
rationales.F12: The small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum is highly suggestive of a mechanical obstruction, which could be due to various causes including adhesions or a mass.
